Seminar Title:

Study on alumina–spinel castable: preformed and insitu spinel

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Ceramic Engineering

Speaker Name:

Satyam Kumar ( Rollno : 519cr1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

CR Department Seminar Hall ( virtual mode)

Date and Time:

29 May 2026 10 am

Contact:

Prof. Ritwik Sarkar ( Intercom. 2203)

Abstract:

Alumina spinel castable, containing pre-reacted and in situ spinel, is becoming increasingly important for steel ladle lining due to its unique combination of properties, including high refractoriness, low porosity, excellent hot strength, good resistance to thermal shock, superior corrosion resistance, etc. In the present work, a high-alumina spinel-containing castable is studied using pre-formed and in-situ spinel. The work is planned to study the effect of different particle size distributions, namely vibratable and self-flowing consistency; effect of spinel content using varying amounts of preformed spinel and fine magnesia respectively; effect of flow modifier (fume silica) content; effect of addition of alumina dispersants (no fume silica containing), effect of property-enhancing additives, etc. Castable compositions are processed conventionally, and vibratable and self-flow compositions were studied using a distribution coefficient (as per Dinger and Funk model) of 0.29 and 0.21, and the castables are evaluated at 110, 1000, and 1550 ˚C for the various refractory properties. Slightly lower density and strength values are found for castables with in-situ spinel composition, due to volume expansion associated with spinel formation.
